examples.question_text: Find the area enclosed by $y=x^{2}$ and $y=x+12$.
Find the area of the region bounded by $y=x^{2}$, $y=(x-8)^{2}$ and the $x$-axis.
Find the area of the region bounded by $y=x^{2}$, $y=4(x-9)^{2}$ and the $x$-axis.

methods.description: Solve for the intersections, identify the upper curve and integrate upper minus lower over the enclosed interval.
methods.sourceRef: booklets/mathsmap-sources/Stage 6 Extension 1/Further Applications of Calculus 3_Area between curves and volumes of revolution.md lines 706–717, Rotating Area between Two Curves, Development question 4(a)

methods.description: Identify the axis intercepts and the crossing where the boundary changes; integrate each curve above the axis over its applicable interval and add the areas.
methods.sourceRef: booklets/mathsmap-sources/Stage 6 Extension 1/Further Applications of Calculus 3_Area between curves and volumes of revolution.md lines 751–759, Rotating Area between Two Curves, Development question 6(a)

methods.description: When algebra gives additional intersections, use the axis intercepts and the requested region to select the crossing that bounds the axis-adjacent region before splitting its area.

examples.derivation: Solving x²=4(x−9)² gives 3(x−6)(x−18)=0. The axis intercepts are 0 and 9, so the axis-adjacent region uses x=6. Its area is ∫₀⁶x² dx + ∫₆⁹4(x−9)² dx = 72+36 = 108 square units. The plotted boundaries, shading and split agree with this region. Moving the label to (10,46), anchored right, preserves all mathematics and places it beyond both plotted curves.
